title: Improving your hormonal profile naturally: train hard & frequently
summary: Starts a series on improving natural hormone levels. NH argues small hormonal edges compound over years for naturals; any physical activity helps, but heavy, challenging lifting (especially squats and deadlifts) best stimulates testosterone/GH, and a gym where you can own your space and lift aggressively matters. Size, strength and hormones grow in synergy.

claims.claim: Hormonal profile matters for naturals because it affects muscle gain and fat distribution; small edges compound like the difference between 4 and 5 sets repeated over 365 days a year for years.
Active men tend to be healthier and more energetic with higher male hormones; this is plausible but not well enough studied to be empirical proof, so observe life around you.
Any physical activity (swimming, running, climbing, dancing) helps hormone production; you don't have to lift weights.
Lifting in ranges that truly challenge you gives the greatest hormonal boost; if you stay in an unchallenging range the body only repairs damage and has no reason to raise testosterone.

Low-rep work on some lifts is worthwhile; studies show acute testosterone and GH increases after heavy lifts, especially squats and deadlifts, small but adding up when repeated several times a week for years.
Free testosterone climbs until around age 35-40, after which any extra you can encourage is beneficial.
Train in a gym that lets you go 100% and lift how you want; a restrictive gym reduces your ability to lift heavy and, he believes, hurts hormone production.
He cites a study suggesting expansive, space-taking postures raise testosterone in men; owning your space in the gym matters, which crowded commercial gyms prevent.

Strength, size and hormonal profile grow in a positive loop for naturals: more hormones, more muscle, heavier lifting, more hormones. Natural bodybuilding still has untapped potential with diligent work.

exercises.name: Squat / deadlift (heavy)
exercises.why: heavy lifts linked to acute testosterone and GH increases
